n: Mouriya Honten (モーリヤ本店, Kobe)
w: Kobe's oldest beef house (founded 1885); the Sannomiya flagship grills A5 Kobe beef teppanyaki at the counter. Listed in the Kobe Beef council's official restaurant guide (JNTO-hosted) and recommended by Inside Kyoto.

n: Steakland Kobe-kan (ステーキランド神戸館)
address: 6F Sannomiya Kogyo Bldg., 1-9-17 Kitanagasa-dori, Chuo-ku, Kobe, Hyogo
w: The affordable way into Kobe beef: teppanyaki steak sets (premium tenderloin with soup, salad, veg, dessert and coffee) a minute from Hankyu Sannomiya. Named in the official Kobe Beef restaurant guide and by Inside Kyoto.

dish: Kobe beef teppanyaki steak with garlic
address: 1F Hillside Terrace, 1-22-13 Nakayamate-dori, Chuo-ku, Kobe, Hyogo
w: Kitano-chō teppanyaki house where chefs grill Kobe beef with butter and garlic before you; Inside Kyoto calls it one of the best places in Kobe to try the city's wagyu, and it is listed in the official Kobe Beef restaurant guide.

n: Freundlieb (フロインドリーブ, Kobe)
w: German bakery founded by Heinrich Freundlieb in 1924, since 1997 housed in the W.M. Vories-designed former Kobe Union Church: cakes, sandwiches and pastries under a vaulted nave.

n: Nishimura Coffee Nakayamate Honten (にしむら珈琲店 中山手本店)
w: Kobe's landmark coffee house since 1948 and one of the first in the city to serve cappuccino and Vienna coffee; on-site roasting and cakes at the Nakayamate main shop.
The shop that put Wakayama ramen on the national map when it won TV Tokyo's 'Japan's best ramen' battle in 1998; porky tonkotsu-shōyu chūka soba, eaten with self-serve hayazushi mackerel sushi.

n: Mitsumori Honpo (三津森本舗, Arima Onsen)
w: The original maker of Arima's tansan senbei — 1 mm wafers baked by hand with the town's carbonated spring water — on the main Yumotozaka street; the adjoining Mitsumori Cafe serves senbei French toast.

n: Ichiju Nisai Ueno Minoten (一汁二菜うえの 箕面店)
w: Michelin-listed (2026 guide) Japanese restaurant at the foot of the Minoh mountains, near the Minoo Park trailhead.
